doc.title: Phil Schaap interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003

title: Steven K. Nenno and the Fletcher Henderson Festival
summary: WABC's ratings man discovers KCR ranked seventh in New York during the Henderson festival.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: ’73 I did the Fletcher Henderson Festival. And then okay, fine. And I get this phone call and says “I am Steven K. Nenno” — this is WABC who had a radio network at the time — “I’m in charge of, you know Arbitron is one thing but we do our own radio listings. And I need to talk to you. I’d like to come to WKCR and check out your operation.” So you know I’m 22 at the time, this could be big. He’s not the police, I’m not going to get arrested, or what could he do to me? So I go yeah. So he shows up and he literally sniffs around the joint and finally he tells me what’s the bottom line. He says, “Well you know I am Steven K. Nenno” he always said his name — the four times I heard him say his name with the middle initial — “I am Steven K. Nenno and I do these in-house ratings for the WABC radio people. And I had to see this for myself. You see in the first week of December of 1973 the seventh most listened to radio station in New York City was on a radio station I never heard of, a radio program I had never heard of, about a person I had never heard of, broadcast by a person I had never heard of.”

Yeah. I mean KCR had never popped up in his chart. So he had to go look in his FM code book to find it’s the Columbia University FM station. First of all FM stations didn’t pop up too often in the charts yet. So what are they doing? They had a Beatles festival? Whatever he thinks. First of all no, it’s not the Beatles, it’s not the Rolling Stones, there’s not a Jimi Hendrix memorial, it’s the Fletcher Henderson festival. Okay who’s Fletcher Henderson? He may be a coming pop college star. I better find out about him. No, the broadcast was by a college guy, Phil Schaap. Oh well who’s he? Well who’s Fletcher Henderson? What’s a Fletcher Henderson festival? How did they pop up seventh? You’ve never been on our listings ever. I mean you never even like a subscriber — however they — no one ever said WKCR to us. And this week we got seventh. You’re seventh. The seventh most listened to radio show that week in New York City. Who the hell are you and what is this all about? And then I knew that the Bird Festival was in August and September of ’73. The Fletcher Henderson Festival was the first week in December ’73. And that’s the thing. And Bird’s — Fletcher Henderson proved it but Bird did the work. Him and Lennie Tristano and Irv Shenkler.
No I was 22 when that happened. ’73.
So how many years have you been on the air?
I’ve been on the air from February 2 of ’70. For 3-1/2 years I had been at KCR at this transition. And from then it’s big time. It’s a big deal.
And that’s Bird. Like I say so Bird seems to be — so I dwelt on that and never relinquished the desire to continue letting him be the crusader.
